# Performance report

*Report* · also written Search Console Performance report

The Search Console report of clicks, impressions, click-through rate and position for a site's queries and pages.

Narrative: the topic [Working with Search Console data](../topics/search-console-data.md) tells the story; this card lists what links to it.

17 claims mention it: 3 from Google's documentation, 10 shown or said at the event (4 confirmed by Google docs, 5 consistent with Google docs, 1 nothing to verify), 4 the author's analysis. A card is a map: cite the claim ids, with the citation given after each claim.

## Google's documentation

Documented in: [Performance report (Search results): Overview and basic setup](https://support.google.com/webmasters/answer/7576553?hl=en), [Performance report (Search results): Advanced filtering and comparison](https://support.google.com/webmasters/answer/17011165?hl=en), [What are impressions, position, and clicks?](https://support.google.com/webmasters/answer/7042828?hl=en).

- [`D1-C264`](../sessions/D1-S04-lightning-session-a-automation-and-ai.md) Docs: Search Console Help defines position as the position of a link on Google, where 1 is the topmost position, and says the Performance report shows the topmost position a property's link occupied, averaged across all queries. `[D1-C264, docs, Google Search Console Help, https://support.google.com/webmasters/answer/7042828?hl=en]`
- [`D3-C465`](../sessions/D3-S12-inside-search-console-what-s-new-how-to-use-it.md) Docs: Google's announcement of 24 September 2026 says multimodal search data appears both in the Performance report for Search results and in the generative AI performance report, can be exported, and began rolling out globally that day. `[D3-C465, docs, Search Central blog (24 September 2026), https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2026/09/web-multimodal-in-sc]`
- [`D3-C498`](../sessions/D3-S13-lightning-session-l-understanding-serps-and-your-users.md) Docs: Google's AI features guide says traffic from sites appearing in AI features such as AI Overviews and AI Mode is included in the overall search traffic in Search Console and reported in the Performance report within the Web search type. `[D3-C498, docs, Google Search Central, https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features]`

## Shown or said at the event

Not in Google's documentation first: present those as said at Search Central Live, never as documented policy.

- [`D3-C429`](../sessions/D3-S12-inside-search-console-what-s-new-how-to-use-it.md) Stage, Day 3, confirmed by Google docs: Search Console's AI-powered configuration is a chat box in which users describe the analysis they want in natural language, and the request is transformed into the Performance report's configuration. `[D3-C429, stage, Ariel Kroszynski, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C431`](../sessions/D3-S12-inside-search-console-what-s-new-how-to-use-it.md) Stage, Day 3, confirmed by Google docs: Search Console's AI-powered configuration lists the changes it will make to the Performance report and applies them only after the user approves. `[D3-C431, stage, Ariel Kroszynski, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C438`](../sessions/D3-S12-inside-search-console-what-s-new-how-to-use-it.md) Stage, Day 3, confirmed by Google docs: The regular Search Console Performance report still shows all traffic including AI features, while the generative AI view shows only impressions from AI surfaces. `[D3-C438, stage, Ariel Kroszynski, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C451`](../sessions/D3-S12-inside-search-console-what-s-new-how-to-use-it.md) Stage, Day 3, confirmed by Google docs: In a YouTube platform property, long-form and short-form videos can be compared in the Performance report's comparison mode by URL pattern, /watch versus /shorts/; Instagram posts (/p/) and reels can be compared the same way. `[D3-C451, stage, Ariel Kroszynski, Day 3]`
- [`D1-C463`](../sessions/D1-S12-q-a.md) Stage, Day 1, consistent with Google docs: A Google panelist said adding a report that is a variation of the Performance report to the Search Console API would be easier than adding crawl stats, because the Performance report is already in the API. `[D1-C463, stage, Google, Day 1]`
- [`D3-C423`](../sessions/D3-S12-inside-search-console-what-s-new-how-to-use-it.md) Stage, Day 3, consistent with Google docs: Drilling into a query group opens the Search Console Performance report with a regex filter that contains all the queries of the group, so each individual query can be analysed. `[D3-C423, stage, Ariel Kroszynski, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C428`](../sessions/D3-S12-inside-search-console-what-s-new-how-to-use-it.md) Stage, Day 3, consistent with Google docs: Users often told Google that the Search Console Performance report is complex to configure, because it can be filtered and customised in many ways, such as by query, page, country and search type. `[D3-C428, stage, Ariel Kroszynski, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C457`](../sessions/D3-S12-inside-search-console-what-s-new-how-to-use-it.md) Stage, Day 3, consistent with Google docs: Until the multimodal launch, the Search Console Performance report essentially showed only text-based searches. `[D3-C457, stage, Ariel Kroszynski, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C459`](../sessions/D3-S12-inside-search-console-what-s-new-how-to-use-it.md) Stage, Day 3, consistent with Google docs: To see multimodal traffic in the Search Console Performance report, select the multimodal search type instead of the default text-based one. `[D3-C459, stage, Ariel Kroszynski, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C412`](../sessions/D3-S12-inside-search-console-what-s-new-how-to-use-it.md) Stage, Day 3, nothing to verify: Google's Search Console talk at the Deep Dive covered five Search Console launches of the past year: query groups, AI-powered configuration of the Performance report, generative AI control and reporting, platform properties for social accounts, and multimodal search reporting. `[D3-C412, stage, Ariel Kroszynski, Day 3]`

## The author's analysis

- [`D3-C095`](../sessions/D3-S03-making-sense-of-users-queries.md) Analysis: No Google documentation states that fan-out queries stay out of Search Console, but the docs fit the stage statement: the Performance report counts AI Overviews and AI Mode under the user's own queries, and the Generative AI reports have no query dimension. `[D3-C095, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`
- [`D3-C435`](../sessions/D3-S12-inside-search-console-what-s-new-how-to-use-it.md) Analysis: Review the filters and regexes that Search Console's AI-powered configuration proposes before trusting the numbers: Google's launch post calls the feature experimental, warns that AI can misinterpret requests, and limits it to the Search results Performance report (not Discover or News) and to configuration, not sorting or exporting. `[D3-C435, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`
- [`D3-C462`](../sessions/D3-S12-inside-search-console-what-s-new-how-to-use-it.md) Analysis: Google's Performance report help says the queries dimension is not available for the multimodal search type, because these searches mostly use images, so judge image-led traffic by page, country and device, and make product and article images distinctive enough for Lens to match. `[D3-C462, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`
- [`D3-C484`](../sessions/D3-S13-lightning-session-l-understanding-serps-and-your-users.md) Analysis: A query reaches Search Console's Performance report only through an impression, so queries cannot come before impressions; what rises first after a publish or refresh is the number of queries with a few impressions each, before total impressions and clicks grow noticeably. `[D3-C484, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`
